paper_metadata.title: Universal Quantum Speedup for Branch-and-Bound, Branch-and-Cut, and Tree-Search Algorithms
paper_metadata.venue: arXiv preprint (Global Technology Applied Research, JPMorgan Chase)

summary: Introduces Incremental-Quantum-Branch-and-Bound (IQB&B), a quantum algorithm offering universal ~quadratic speedup over classical Branch-and-Bound/Cut/tree-search for every input: if classical B&B has complexity Q with solution depth d, IQB&B achieves O~(sqrt(Q)*d). Applicability covers depth-based, cost-based, and A* heuristics, matching commercial MIP solvers (Gurobi/CPLEX). Numerical study on three MIPs establishes Q >> d empirically: (i) Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model (50 instances, n=20-36), (ii) Maximum Independent Set on Erdos-Renyi graphs (20 instances, n=170-290), and (iii) cardinality-constrained mean-variance portfolio optimization (200 instances, n=32-56 assets). For the portfolio problem, measured node-count complexity is O(2^{0.195 n}) for Gurobi and O(2^{0.140 n}) for CPLEX; IQB&B's projected complexity is O~(2^{0.098 n}) and O~(2^{0.070 n}) respectively. Tree depth is empirically O(n^2). No hardware run or circuit-level simulation: the quantum complexity numbers are obtained by applying the proven sqrt speedup to the measured classical Q values.

experiments.description: Empirical evaluation of classical MIP solver node counts on a cardinality- and diversification-constrained mean-variance portfolio optimization, used to project Incremental-Quantum-Branch-and-Bound (IQB&B) performance. 200 random instances per n in {32, ..., 56} assets; mu, Sigma, Pi (prices) generated randomly; objective min x^T Sigma x - mu^T x s.t. Pi^T x = B (budget), ||x||_0 = n/2 (cardinality), Pi_i x_i < 0.1 B (diversification), x in N^{n-1} x R_q. Classical solvers: Gurobi and CPLEX. Quantum result is the paper's theorem applied to measured classical Q: O~(sqrt(Q)*d) with d = O(n^2).

algorithm.variant: Incremental-Quantum-Branch-and-Bound (IQB&B); quantum Branch-and-Bound using quantum minimum-finding / amplitude amplification a la Montanaro, with incremental tree exploration that matches classical depth-based, cost-based, and A* heuristics

hyperparameters.diversification_constraint: Pi_i * x_i < 0.1 * B for all i

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Mean-variance MIP with integer lot variables and cardinality constraint; solved classically by commercial MIP solvers to obtain node-count Q(n); quantum speedup applied analytically as O~(sqrt(Q)*d).
problem_formulation.constraints: budget, cardinality (n/2), diversification (<10% of budget per asset)

dataset_specification.description: 200 random instances per problem size n in {32,...,56}. mu, Sigma, Pi randomly generated. Cardinality fixed at n/2.

speedup_claims.magnitude: near-quadratic in Q (solver node count); specifically O~(sqrt(Q)*d) with d = O(n^2)
speedup_claims.notes: Universal quadratic speedup over any classical Branch-and-Bound / Branch-and-Cut / heuristic tree search. For portfolio: exponent roughly halved (0.195 -> 0.098 with Gurobi; 0.140 -> 0.070 with CPLEX).

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O~(sqrt(Q) * d) node expansions for IQB&B where Q is classical node count and d is tree depth; for portfolio O~(2^{0.098 n}) and O~(2^{0.070 n}) based on Gurobi/CPLEX measurements.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(2^{0.195 n}) (Gurobi) and O(2^{0.140 n}) (CPLEX) median node counts on random mean-variance cardinality-constrained portfolio MIPs.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires fault-tolerant quantum computer capable of coherent amplitude-amplification / quantum minimum-finding over classical MIP-solver state (no resource estimate given in paper).

notes: All numeric complexity exponents from Table 1 and Section 3.3.
Tree-depth scaling d = O(n^2) from Figure 1(c).
